outcome: Type of cesarean sections (urgent vs planned)
cohort: The study included 58 women aged 32.3 ± 3.5 years with a body mass index 22.9 ± 3.4 kg/m2 who had large isthmocele with residual myometrial thickness <3 mm and secondary infertility.
finding: Surgical treatment for isthmocele in women with secondary infertility resulted in pregnancy in 62.1% and healthy baby delivery in 44.8% of women, with both laparoscopic and laparotomic approaches offering comparable pregnancy outcomes.
mod_finding: There were no differences between the laparoscopic and laparotomic surgical approach groups regarding the number of performed cesarean sections or the type of cesarean sections (urgent vs planned).
